baseline.rationale: Feedback from planning-002: goal_nuts ran only twice and do_pickup/do_tighten once each; the second pass found no useable spanner reachable from the nut location and bailed. The nut location is a sink in the directed link graph (shed->loc1->...->gate, no link out of gate), so a man who walks to the nuts can never fetch another spanner, yet three nuts each consume one spanner. The only consistent resolution is that walking is effectively available in both directions along a link pair, so I compute the adjacency as the symmetric closure of link (still only traversing edges that appear as link facts, never inventing new location pairs). I keep directed BFS as a fallback check but prefer symmetric reachability, and I no longer break the inner loop after one tighten - I iterate over every remaining loose goal nut, re-deriving the man's position each time. Each tighten consumes exactly one useable spanner, so the loop terminates.

first.rationale: Rule R01/R04/R05: I checked argument order and types against the domain definition. walk parameters are (?start ?end ?m) and the incumbent emitted "(walk %s %s %s)" with (p[i], p[i+1], m) — consistent. tighten_nut is (?l ?s ?m ?n) and the incumbent emitted (nl, s, m, n) — consistent. So the failure is not argument order; the earliest observed error is plan_semantics on every task with full plan_length (21, 15) far above executed_actions (7, 7), meaning the emitted walk steps stop being executable mid-plan. The concrete defect is R03-violating: the incumbent computes the symmetric closure of the directed link relation ("we traverse a link edge in either direction because otherwise ... dead end"), so every backward walk it emits is illegal. I therefore removed that illegal assumption and instead replaced the hand-written state updates with a faithful STRIPS simulator: successors() enumerates exactly the ground actions whose preconditions hold, so no emitted action can be illegal; BFS over that space returns the shortest legal plan reaching all goal tuples. This also removes the duplicated/hand-maintained effect bookkeeping that could drift from the domain. Alternative explanation considered (R06): that success requires re-visiting nuts in a specific order — but that is subsumed since BFS explores orderings exhaustively. Prediction is on development_successes only, a development observation, not a held-out claim.
